messages:
Maya Patel: Hey team — running into a customer escalation. Their app started getting 403s when calling our inference endpoint after a key rotation yesterday. Error from the client:

```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  \"error\": \"insufficient_scope\",
  \"message\": \"token missing scopes: inference.generate\"
}
```

Repro steps they gave:
1) Replace API key in env `REDWOOD_API_KEY` with the rotated key.
2) Hit `POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` with a small prompt.
3) See 403 above.

They shared the token prefix (redacted): `rk_live_1a2b3c4d` and org `org_9a8b7c6d`. Any ideas?

Liam Chen: thanks @Maya. Quick check — did they create the token via the OAuth app / SSO flow or via the Console -> API tokens page? OAuth app tokens are often scoped at install-time and can omit inference.

Maya Patel: They said they rotated through the SSO provider (Okta) and used our "Login with Redwood" app to mint a token for CI. So likely OAuth path.

Liam Chen: ok. Two likely causes: 1) the new token was created with a narrower scope set (e.g., embeddings only), or 2) the token is an ephemeral OAuth access token that needs additional user consent for inference.

Quick troubleshooting commands for the customer (do not ask them to paste full key):

- Verify scopes attached to the token: (they can run locally if they have the key)
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokens/me
# returns {"scopes": ["embeddings","rerank"]} etc.
```
- Repro with a minimal SDK call to check behavior:
```
import redwood
client = redwood.Client(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
client.generate(model='gpt-redwood-1', prompt='hi')
```
If `tokens/me` shows the missing `inference` scope, that's the issue.

Noah Rivera: I'm pulling audit logs for org_9a8b7c6d now. @deploy-bot can you show the token.create events for that org in the last 48h?

deploy-bot: audit.log:token.create — 2026-03-08T13:42:10Z — actor: okta-integration@customer — scopes: ["embeddings","rerank"] — token_id: tok_04f3...

Noah Rivera: looks like the token was indeed created without `inference`. That matches the 403.

Ava Johnson: flagging this as a customer-impact P1 since production traffic is blocked. @Noah we need the quickest remediation path to share with the customer. Also include instructions so they don't share full keys in the thread.

Liam Chen: remediation options (pick one depending on customer preference):

1) Short-term (fast): Have them create a new service token from Console -> Settings -> API Tokens -> Create token and explicitly select scopes: `inference`, `embeddings`, `rerank`. They should then update their CI secret with the new token.

2) If they must use SSO / OAuth tokens: Update the OAuth app scopes and re-consent the app in their IdP so the token includes `inference`. For Okta this is in the app configuration -> Assignments -> OAuth scopes. After changing, a reinstall/re-consent mint will produce a token with the new scopes.

3) As a fallback, create a short-lived developer token via `redwood tokens create` CLI and give them the prefix to validate (we'll need to ensure they rotate immediately). Example CLI: 
```
redwood tokens create --name "support-temp-inference" --scopes inference,embeddings,rerank --expires 24h
# returns token: rk_live_xxx (only show prefix in thread)
```

How to verify once they have a new token: call `GET /v1/tokens/me` or run the same simple generate request — success should return 200 with a token response body.

Noah Rivera: I posted the audit findings to their account case and I'll draft a short how-to for Okta consent. Also validating there are no server-side bugs that would drop scopes on rotate.

Maya Patel: Customer is okay creating a new token from the Console. I provided the Console path & CLI snippet. I'm going to have them rotate CI secrets and report back.

(15m later)

Maya Patel: Update — they created a new service token from the Console with scopes `inference,embeddings,rerank`. After swapping the secret, their generate calls return 200 and tokens/me shows the correct scopes.

Noah Rivera: Confirmed in audit logs: token.create event shows scopes ["inference","embeddings","rerank"] and a successful call to /v1/generate from their ip.

Ava Johnson: great — marking this resolved on our side. Follow-ups:
- Docs: add a short blurb to the token rotation guide about OAuth/SAML flows and consented scopes.
- Support playbook: include `tokens/me` as first troubleshooting step for 403 insufficient_scope.

Maya Patel: Customer confirmed app in prod is healthy. They'll move forward with SSO scoping changes separately. Thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:

Liam Chen: closing on our side. If they run into anything else, reopen and attach `tokens/me` output (redacted) or the token prefix.

deploy-bot: case 2026-31789 updated -> status: resolved
